tasks.short: Establish and implement cleaning standards and procedures

steps.what: Establish operational standards and procedures for the supervised cleaning department
Document standards and procedures in the controlled departmental instruction format
Implement procedures by explaining, demonstrating and resolving practical staff questions

tasks.design: Configure controlled site-instruction templates in {DOCS}. The supervisor decides the standards, checks the assembled instructions and retains demonstration, implementation and staff questions; templates do not select safe methods automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Formatting repeated instruction sections consumes some time after methods are decided.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates can reuse structure and version details.
tasks.still_hard: Matching service requirements, safe materials and practical site conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor can recognise when an instruction cannot be followed safely in the actual space.
tasks.altitude: Less instruction assembly with standards and implementation responsibility intact.

reach.task: Identify an instruction that conflicts with actual site conditions

evidence.claim: Controlled templates can reduce document assembly while operational standards and practical implementation remain human; this is an unmeasured scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is supervisor standards, documentation and implementation, excluding client contract changes and cleaner execution time.

Supervisor produces site, activity, frequency, method, material, safety limits and required checks in s1 with all 40 hours retained. s2's 15 retained hours include field capture, editing and checking; no ready structured safe method is assumed.
Missing or disputed requirements return to manual site and client clarification. No automatic safety or chemical selection is introduced.
Test native templates before custom code. Existing formatting earns no new gain. All demonstration and staff contact time remains.
unknowns: Current instruction burden and site-specific controls
research_questions: Can templates shorten instruction assembly without hiding site-specific safety differences?

already_counted.description: Instruction entry, editing and source checks

incremental.description: Maintain templates and current site references

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=40+15+40=95; gross 5 minus 2 upkeep gives net 3. High requires repeated formatting; low removes only 2 hours, offset by upkeep. Standards and implementation retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inventory supplies and equipment for adequate availability

steps.what: Inventory physical stock and check usable supplies and equipment condition
Record counted stock quantities, units, locations and condition exceptions
Compare inventory quantities with the current approved stock targets
Check stock gaps and decide the action needed for adequate availability

tasks.design: Configure a stock sheet in {SPREADSHEET} or the existing inventory app {OTHER} to compare supervisor-entered usable counts against approved targets. Physical counting and entry retain all time; the supervisor reviews gaps and equipment exceptions before requesting replenishment or repair.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated stock-to-target arithmetic can follow manual counting and recording.
tasks.enabler_now: Native formulas can compare validated rows without interpreting equipment condition.
tasks.still_hard: Usable condition, missing stock, unit mistakes and whether a nominal target still fits the site.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor can recognise equipment that exists on the list but cannot safely be issued.
tasks.altitude: Remove only repeated comparison arithmetic; counting and availability decisions remain.

reach.task: Flag damaged or unusable stock before it is counted as available

evidence.claim: Native stock comparison formulas can remove repeated arithmetic after reliable count capture; physical counting and availability judgement remain. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is stock inventory and availability assessment, excluding ordering and physical issue to workers.

Supervisor produces item, unit, site, location, usable quantity, count date and condition exceptions in s1 and s2, with all 80 hours retained. s2 validates these exact structured rows before s3 consumes them; no stock feed or condition code is supplied free.

Supervisor maintains target item, unit, site and quantity through existing stock policy; s4's 10 hours include checking target suitability and resolving missing fields. Initial target capture is rollout work and recurring target updates are counted in upkeep.

Missing units, stale counts or absent targets block automatic comparison for that row and return to manual checking in s4. Test native formulas first; current formulas earn no new gain and no order is automatic.
unknowns: Actual comparison effort and existing stock tools
research_questions: Does a checked stock sheet reduce comparison time without overstating usable availability?

incremental.description: Maintain targets, units and formula checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=60+20+0+10=90; gross 10 minus 2 upkeep gives net 8. High requires repeated manual comparison; low removes only 2 hours where most comparisons are exceptions, offset by upkeep. Count capture and availability decisions retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Issue supplies and equipment to workers

steps.what: Issue suitable supplies and equipment to workers and explain relevant limits

tasks.design: Retain physical selection, safe handover and explanation with the supervisor. Existing safe-use instructions may remain in {DOCS}; issuing physical supplies is not replaced by a stock dashboard.
tasks.previous_blocker: The correct item must be physically available and suitable for the worker's actual task.
tasks.enabler_now: Inventory software can show records but does not perform this physical handover.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising unsuitable equipment or materials and explaining safe-use constraints.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor can notice damage or misunderstanding before the equipment reaches the work area.
tasks.altitude: Physical issue time and safety responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Check the issued item against the task and raise concerns before use

evidence.claim: Physical supply issue and safe handover remain work even when inventory records are digital.

assumptions: Boundary is physical issue and explanation, excluding inventory counting, purchase and later worker use.
Supervisor observes the task and item condition during retained s1; no structured safe-to-issue flag is assumed.
Existing stock access is baseline; test native stock functions before future custom work. No separate issue-log paperwork is invented.
No software or maintained process is introduced, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Equipment and material mix and safe-use requirements
research_questions: Are issue delays caused by physical stock location rather than record administration?

already_counted.description: Physical selection, handover and safety explanation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and upkeep=0. Routine and exceptional issue retain physical and explanation time; stock-record gains are counted only in inventory.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Forecast staffing and stock requirements by period

steps.what: Verify site workload, staffing constraints and stock inputs for the forecast
Calculate necessary staffing and stock levels for each forecast period
Evaluate forecast staffing and stock levels and explain scheduling or ordering needs

tasks.design: Configure a scenario calculator in the existing planning module {OPS_SYSTEM} or {SPREADSHEET}, using verified workload and explicit time and consumption assumptions. The supervisor checks period totals and evaluates uncertainty; the forecast does not publish a roster or place orders.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changing workload can require repeated staffing-hours and consumption arithmetic.
tasks.enabler_now: Native formulas and scenarios can recalculate explicit assumptions consistently.
tasks.still_hard: Absence, access constraints, unusual cleaning needs and whether time norms fit actual work.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor can reject a mathematically balanced forecast that ignores real site conditions.
tasks.altitude: Less scenario arithmetic with resource judgement and staff decisions retained.

reach.task: Use the checked resource forecast to discuss feasible coverage

evidence.claim: FacilityApps provides site and employee schedules with working-time and collective-agreement checks; this establishes planning capability, not measured accuracy or labour savings for the proposed resource forecast.
Explicit workload and consumption formulas can reduce repeated forecast arithmetic while assumption choice remains human.

assumptions: Boundary is resource forecasting, excluding roster publication, purchasing, physical stock counting and other staff labour.

Supervisor produces site, room or task type, quantity, frequency, period, planned changes, available hours and checked stock references in s1 with all 30 hours retained. Client provides existing contract scope through unchanged contract work; no new free client data collection is assumed.

Supervisor selects minutes per task, consumption per task, buffer, lead time and unit in s2's 14 retained hours, including capture and formula checks. Initial norms are rollout work and recurring updates are upkeep; no ready accurate productivity or stock-target code is assumed.

Missing workload, stale stock or unsuitable norms require manual scenarios and explicit uncertainty. Test native calculators before custom code; existing recalculation earns no new gain. No model assesses staff performance or assigns shifts.
unknowns: Workload data quality and current forecast arithmetic
Approved norms, collective-agreement rules and consultation needs
research_questions: Can scenario recalculation reduce preparation while forecasts remain accurate enough for safe coverage and usable stock?

already_counted.description: Norm selection, formula checking and manual exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain workload norms, stock assumptions and rule versions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=30+14+35=79; gross 21 minus 4 upkeep gives net 17. High requires repeated scenario arithmetic with reliable inputs; low removes only 4 hours under unstable workload, offset by upkeep. Input verification and forecast judgement retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce instruction assembly and explicit stock or workload arithmetic while keeping physical work, standards and resource judgement with the supervisor.
reach: Help cleaners report usable condition and planners understand the assumptions behind coverage needs
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor who uses checked counts and transparent resource calculations while remaining present for safe cleaning work and staff needs.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Housekeeping and Janitorial Workers
